title: Dorsett Waterfront Subang: a lake view built for short stays.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #471 | DORSETT WATERFRONT SUBANG, SUBANG JAYA
excerpt: A Subang Jaya high-rise beside Dorsett Grand, facing the Subang Ria lake park, designed for short and medium stays rather than own-stay families.
takeaways: Unblocked lake and golf course views from the balconies, next to the Dorsett Grand Subang hotel.
Built for short stays: a hotel-style lobby, six fast passenger lifts and wide corridors, with studios asking about RM2,100 to RM2,300 a month furnished.
More than 2,000 units, an underused facility deck and a confusing layout are the trade-offs.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Dorsett Waterfront Subang is two large towers on commercial title, more than 2,000 units in all, run alongside the Dorsett hotel next door. It has a hotel-style lobby, six passenger lifts and a service lift, and 2 m-wide corridors, though these have no voids and rely on artificial light.

There are mainly two layouts: a 570 sq ft unit with a separate bedroom, and two-bedroom units at the corners. The unit Sean tours is 3.85 m wide, with a bathtub and a 1.7 m balcony looking over the lake. The level 4 facility deck has three pools, a gym, a games room and a playground.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It is in SS12, beside Dorsett Grand Subang and Subang Jaya Medical Centre, looking over the Taman Subang Ria lake park towards a golf course, with the park's cafes a walk away. The pocket has always been private, with one way in, and a new direct turn-in from the Federal Highway now makes it far easier to reach, with an LRT station at the new township opposite.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Units like the one Sean visits are listed at about RM900 psf, or around RM516,000. Furnished, they ask about RM2,100 to RM2,300 a month, some up to RM2,500, and the corner two-bedrooms, which are in demand, about RM3,500 to RM3,600.

Tenants range from short-stay guests to students and medium-term professionals, and Sean saw both luggage and laundry on the balconies. He suggests furnishing fully at minimum cost so a unit can serve any of them, and says the numbers still make sense as an investment.

standout.title: A deck that runs along the lake
standout.body: The facility deck stretches the length of the building behind an unbroken glass balustrade facing Taman Subang Ria and its lake, which Sean calls the reason the project will work. Six fast lifts deal with the usual complaint in a building this size.

pros: A strategic location: a private, one-way-in pocket of Subang Jaya that now has a direct turn-in from the Federal Highway, links to other highways and an LRT station nearby, with universities, malls, hospitals, schools and clubs all around.
Dorsett as the hotel partner: the brand draws people to the project, and guests who don't want to pay hotel prices can stay next door, so residents benefit from the hotel's overflow.

Designed in detail for its audience: once you see it is meant for short stays, the big lobby, the six fast lifts, the 2 m corridors with a lake-facing opening, the wider-than-usual units, the roomy bedroom and the balcony all make sense, and its ratings on booking platforms are decent.
cons: Density: more than 2,000 units in two massive blocks, which he thinks makes it the densest project in Subang Jaya.

Execution: the facility deck and lobby are so large they feel empty. The original specification is good, with glass railings, three pools and a rooftop, but Sean suspects, without being sure, that the project nearly stalled and was finished in a rush.

A confusing design: an entrance that doesn't read as one, a car park shared by hotel guests and residents, back-of-house transitions to the lift lobby, a kindergarten that is a label on an empty room, and units that feel dark once the bedroom door is closed. It becomes easier once you know the building.

closing: An investment unit for students, short stays and medium-term tenants in a location with deep demand; hard to recommend as an own-stay family home.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this September 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the unit, which had just been rented out; prices and rents are asking figures as he quoted them.
